name: feature-loop
description: Write a new feature/function as a vertical CQRS slice: lock the scope -> outward from the domain -> test in step
pattern: vertical slice, verify after each layer
whenToUse: Adding a feature, endpoint, function, or a new agent tool.
whenNotToUse: The request is still vague at the business level -> write an SRS first. Changing existing code -> fixbug-loop.

steps.goal: Lock the scope BEFORE typing a line
outputs: DON'T: <the adjacent thing deliberately left alone>
steps.exitCriteria: The three lines are written down. Anywhere two readings lead to substantially different work => ASK, do not guess.
steps.note: The most common failure mode at this step is not writing the wrong thing - it is writing TOO MUCH.

steps.goal: Put the code in the right project
steps.exitCriteria: Domain -> HW.Domain | the feature's CQRS + agent tools -> HW.Application/Features/<F>/ | EF/store -> HW.Infrastructure | controller/DI -> HW.Api | tests -> HW.UnitTests
steps.note: Only put something in HW.Agentic if it is right for EVERY application. A test blocks it from referencing back up: HW.UnitTests/Agentic/AgenticIsolationTests.cs

steps.goal: Follow the shape that exists, do not invent a new one
outputs: The template file that was read
steps.exitCriteria: At least one comparable feature has been read (Features/Vocabs/ is the most complete template)
steps.note: New code must read like the code around it: same comment density, same naming, same idioms.

steps.goal: Invariants belong to the domain, not to the handler
steps.exitCriteria: Build green + domain tests for every invariant and every domain event
Handler tests: happy + not-found + one boundary case. Validator tests: one test per rule.
steps.note: Queries do NOT open transactions. Long-running work (agents, fan-out) makes that more important, not less.

steps.exitCriteria: Needs a migration => STOP and ASK FOR APPROVAL. A migration is an irreversible action.

outputs: DI registration in the feature's ServiceCollectionExtensions
steps.note: Going the other way (controller first) almost always leaks DTOs back into the domain.

steps.exitCriteria: PASS, and nothing outside the DO: line was touched

steps.goal: A second pair of eyes before declaring done
steps.exitCriteria: The surrounding code was read before judging

stopConditions.rule: editing a file that is not on the DO: line
stopConditions.action: Stop. Record it under 'Seen but not touched', do not fix it.

stopConditions.rule: needs a migration / schema change / data deletion
stopConditions.action: Stop and ask for approval. Do not do it and report afterwards.

stopConditions.rule: two readings lead to substantially different work
stopConditions.action: Ask one question. Cheaper than 300 wrong lines.
